mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and increasing the present value of S&P 500 earnings, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods when FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against a zero mean return.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 8.5% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a flight to safety and reduces equity risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by >0.3pp over 3 months, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) signals weak aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, as evidenced by a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production below 95.0 (index 2017=100) indicates a contraction in real output, which signals a weakening economy and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls below 95.0, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% annually and the federal funds rate remains below 1.0%, it indicates a lagging monetary response to inflation, increasing real rate uncertainty and reducing equity valuations, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL > 2.5% yoy and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, as shown by a t-test p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate, signals strong labor market momentum that may trigger inflationary expectations and preemptive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds 200k and UNRATE declines, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 330,000 million dollars, combined with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 500,000 units, indicates a collapse in consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of RSAFS < 330000 and HOUST < 500 fails to predict negative 20-day SPX returns, as shown by a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0, occurring during a period of rising unemployment (UNRATE > 8.5%), signals a supply-side contraction driven by demand collapse, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO < 95.0 and UNRATE > 8.5%, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05.
